Interpret tree calculation and volume codes

Source: R/utils.R
status_codes.Rd

Return calculation codes, names, meanings, and sources for stem and merchandising results.

Usage

## Call signatures
status_codes()

Value

A data frame with integer code, character name, character category, character description, and character source. All fields are unitless. Code identifies the diagnosis, name gives its stable label, category groups related problems, description explains the code, and source identifies the calculation group.

No values are user defaults.

Details

Row codes describe individual calculations. Invalid argument structure can stop a call before row codes are assigned. The literal descriptions returned by this lookup retain some development wording.

Coordinate and source codes

outside_divisions, outside_divisions, means the coordinate lookup found no shipped ecological division. Its value is missing. Check coordinates and coverage.

library_error_base is the offset added to positive source error numbers. The calculated quantity is unavailable.

Correct the equation's required measurements and geographic selection before repeating the calculation.

Status and missing values

Structural errors stop the call. Row failures return missing values unless a retained-value case is explicitly identified below. na_input is silent with status = FALSE, while other nonzero codes produce warnings.

ok

Calculation completed. The value is usable within the selected equation's scope.

na_input

A required value is missing or nonfinite. Supply the measurement before using this row.

dbh_nonpositive

Tree diameter is not positive. Correct the diameter and rerun.

ht_nonpositive

Total height is not positive. Correct the height and rerun.

unknown_species

The supplied species code is invalid or unrecognized for this operation. Correct it.

unknown_model

No equation was found. Check the identifier or register the local equation.

missing_input

An equation requires an omitted input or complete measurement pair. Supply it and rerun.

species_out_of_scope

A value is retained for a species outside the declared scope. Review equation suitability before reporting.

capability_missing

The requested calculation is unavailable, often because outside-bark information is absent. Supply a supported bark ratio or choose another equation.

kernel_error

The equation calculation failed to evaluate. The result is missing. Check the tree and equation separately.

h_out_of_range

A height is below ground or above total height. Check height units and bounds.

diameter_nonpositive

The target diameter is not positive. Supply a positive target or use the tip bound for volume.

empty_bounds

The lower height is not below the upper height. Correct the interval. The missing result is not a measured zero volume.

above_tip

The requested diameter is smaller than the modeled tip diameter. Revise the target.

below_stump

The requested diameter exceeds the modeled diameter at stump. Revise the target or stump convention.

not_unique

The profile has another diameter crossing below the returned height. The highest crossing is retained. Review whether it matches the intended utilization limit.

no_convergence

The numerical search did not converge. Review the target and profile before using the tree.

Source equation errors retain their library diagnosis. Those values are unavailable.

Check the selected equation and its inputs. Zero volume or diameter can be a modeled boundary value. These functions do not select logs, so a zero is not evidence of merchantable zero volume.

With status = TRUE, trees$status and logs$status are integer columns. ok means the calculation completed. no_feasible_log means a valid tree produced no feasible log.

Other failures require review before summarizing. A failed tree can retain partial output, so its presence in a log table does not establish a complete result.

The merchandising codes are:

no_entry_product

No product passed tree eligibility. Review species, diameter classes, age, and pruning requirements.

defect_height_out_of_range

A defect height is outside the tree. Check its units and reference to ground.

defect_interval_invalid

Defect bounds are invalid.

Check the interval and point-record conventions.

defect_percent_out_of_range

A percentage is outside zero through 100. Correct the recorded percentage.

model_unresolved

No equation was resolved for the species. Check the species and equation map.

unknown_defect_effect

The effect is unsupported.

Use one of the documented operational treatments.

unknown_curvature_category

A category is absent from the ordered scale. Reconcile category labels.

missing_product_attribute

A product needs a missing tree attribute. Supply it or revise the product requirement.

utilization_top_invalid

The requested top cannot be resolved.

Check the diameter, bark basis, and equation.

no_feasible_log

Valid zero volume under these specifications. Retain the tree in inventory counts.

scale_input_unavailable

A scaling measurement cannot be calculated. Check species, bark information, and measurement inputs.

Missing scaled quantity and dependent value remain NA.

profile_adapter_failure

Profile evaluation or the calculation plan failed. Inspect diagnostics and reproduce the tree separately before treating the result as usable.

reconciliation_failure

The volume accounting did not close. Investigate the tree and model before reporting totals.

Some invalid defect and product inputs are caught earlier and stop the call instead of becoming tree codes. Equation failures retain the input, model, capability, and evaluation diagnoses returned by status_codes().

Before calculating totals, count statuses across the complete tree table. Do not silently drop failed trees or interpret missing quantities as zero. product_summary() defaults to excluding missing quantities from sums.

Use na_action = 'propagate' when an incomplete sum should remain missing. A log-table summary alone cannot count trees having no logs.

See also

merchandise() for tree and log diagnoses, dib() for diameter diagnoses, stand_table() for separating failed trees in expanded totals.

Examples

## Load dplyr
library(dplyr)

## Inspect merchandising diagnoses
status_codes() %>%
  filter(source == 'merchandising') %>%
  slice_head(n = 3)
#>   code                       name category
#> 1  400           no_entry_product  product
#> 2  401 defect_height_out_of_range   defect
#> 3  402    defect_interval_invalid   defect
#>                                        description        source
#> 1         no product passes the static entry rules merchandising
#> 2     a defect height is outside the physical tree merchandising
#> 3 a defect interval has invalid or reversed bounds merchandising
